negativeResult.collection: Dorchester town records, First Church of Dorchester records, Suffolk County Court records 1671-1680, and the Margery Laver will abstract (NEHGR 13)
limitations: All four record streams are printed/OCR editions, not manuscript images; the underlying town and church books were not read directly.

The identification rests on internal consistency across the four sources (the same spelling drift, the same family, the same Burge-surname collision) rather than a single explicit clerk statement equating 'Gurney' and 'Gurnell'.
Coverage is bounded to Dorchester's own town, church, and the one county-court page examined; it does not test other towns for a similar Gurney-Gurnell confusion.
negativeResult.provider: Boston Record Commissioners (printed town-record series); First Church of Dorchester (printed church record); Colonial Society of Massachusetts (printed county-court series); New England Historical and Genealogical Register
negativeResult.queryDescription: Full variant sweep (Gurney/Gurnell/Gornell/Gurnet and related colonial spellings) of the Dorchester town book, First Church of Dorchester records, the Suffolk County Court's 1676/7 Prise surety entry, and the Margery Laver will, testing whether any genuinely distinct Gurney household existed at colonial Dorchester.

incoming.explanation: The Laver will's "Jane Gurnet" legacy is one of the two record threads the negative result resolves.
The three-source Gornell/Gurnell record stream is the primary basis for the negative result.
The one-Gurney-household claim depends on the Dorchester records belonging to the unrelated Gurnell family.

shortLabel: Negative: no true Gurney household at colonial Dorchester

sources.locator: town book spelling series and Jane Gornell footnote
p. 13, "Jane Gurnet" legacy, resolved as Jane Gornell

statement: No independent Gurney household existed at colonial Dorchester. Both the 1664 "Jane Gurnet" legacy and the 1676/7 "Goodman Gurney of Dorchester" surety resolve to the Gornell/Gurnell family under ordinary clerk-level spelling drift, confirmed across three independent Dorchester record streams; no Dorchester "Gurney" record should be read as evidence of John Gurney-1's family.
